As for rally driving - it's pretty fun. I'll try to put it into words.

When you apply your brakes, about 70% of the stopping power goes to the front brakes and the remainder goes to the rear. So, you "load" your brakes by pressing on them and then, just a brief moment later, you use your gas pedal while continuing to apply the brakes. This is known as loading and what this does is it allows your rear tires to spin (more easily and with more control) while you do things like corner.

This is how you throw your ass out sideways when rally driving. Before you get to the corner (you have a co-driver), you load your brakes and get the ass out a little - keeping it under control. When you hit the corner, you are already a little sideways but you increase the rear wheel spin which throws the ass out even more. Doing this properly means you can hit the apex and keep your wheels at speed so you can exit the corner a bit faster as you lose less momentum in the drive train.

The practice cars have bowls on the hoods and they put an orange in the bowl. Your goal is to do this loading the brakes and cornering while keeping the orange in the bowl. It's harder than it sounds but you feel so accomplished when you finally master it.

It's pretty close - it's just down the road in New Hampshire. It's called the Team O'Neil Rally School and it's in Dalton - not too far from Jefferson, on the back side of the White Mountain. That's where Mt. Washington is - which I can see out my front windows.
